config.title: WebSocket Hook

intro.title: WebSocket Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Angular service that manages a WebSocket connection to a real-time server. You'll learn how to use the WebSocket API to send and receive messages, handling events like opening, closing, and errors. The core concept involves creating an observable stream from WebSocket events using RxJS, allowing components to subscribe to live data updates. You'll implement this in TypeScript within an Angular service, focusing on connection management and data flow. By the end, you'll have a functional hook-like service that any component can use for real-time communication.
intro.usecase: WebSocket hooks are essential for building real-time features in modern web applications. You'll use them in live dashboards that display stock prices, sports scores, or IoT sensor data that updates continuously without page refreshes. They power collaborative tools like Google Docs where multiple users edit simultaneously, and chat applications where messages appear instantly. As an Angular developer, implementing WebSocket hooks allows you to create responsive, interactive UIs that maintain persistent connections to servers for live data streaming.

objectives: Initialize a WebSocket connection within an Angular service
Configure WebSocket event listeners to handle incoming messages
Implement a method to send data through the WebSocket connection
Bind WebSocket data to component properties for display
Control the WebSocket lifecycle by managing connection states
Integrate WebSocket error handling to manage connection failures
Manipulate component state based on real-time WebSocket updates

steps.instruction: Import Component, Injectable, and OnDestroy from '@angular/core', and import webSocket from 'rxjs/webSocket'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbols you need from their respective packages.

steps.title: Create a WebSocket service
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular service class named 'WebSocketService' with the @Injectable decorator to handle WebSocket connections.
steps.hint: Use the Angular CLI command 'ng generate service WebSocket' or manually create a service class with @Injectable() decorator.

steps.expectedOutcome: A WebSocketService class with @Injectable decorator is created, ready to encapsulate WebSocket functionality.
successCriteria: WebSocketService class is defined with @Injectable decorator and exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your service has the @Injectable decorator and is exported as a class named WebSocketService.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service wasn't created correctly. Create a class named WebSocketService with the @Injectable decorator.

steps.title: Define WebSocket connection properties
steps.instruction: Inside your WebSocketService class, define a private property named 'socket$' of type WebSocketSubject<string> and a public property named 'webSocketUrl' with the value 'ws://localhost:8080'.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript property declarations with appropriate access modifiers. The WebSocketSubject should be typed for string messages.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WebSocketService will have a private WebSocketSubject property and a public URL property ready for connection setup.
successCriteria: The service contains a private 'socket$' property of type WebSocketSubject<string> and a public 'webSocketUrl' property with the correct URL value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both properties: a private socket$ of type WebSocketSubject<string> and a public webSocketUrl with the URL string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service doesn't have the required properties. You need to define a private socket$ property of type WebSocketSubject<string> and a public webSocketUrl property with the WebSocket URL.

steps.title: Implement WebSocket connection method
steps.instruction: Inside the WebSocketService class, add a public method named connect() that returns a WebSocketSubject observable.
steps.hint: Define the method with a return type of WebSocketSubject<any> (or a more specific type if you prefer). Use the WebSocketSubject constructor to create the connection.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WebSocketService now has a connect method that returns a WebSocketSubject observable for establishing WebSocket connections.
successCriteria: The WebSocketService class contains a public connect() method that returns a WebSocketSubject observable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it's named connect, is public, and returns a WebSocketSubject observable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The connect method is missing or doesn't return a WebSocketSubject observable. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Implement message sending method
steps.instruction: In the WebSocketService class, add a public method named sendMessage that accepts a string parameter and sends it through the WebSocket connection.
steps.hint: Use the WebSocketSubject's next() method to send the message. Remember to add proper TypeScript type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WebSocketService will have a sendMessage method that can send string messages through the WebSocket connection.
successCriteria: The sendMessage method is defined with a string parameter and uses the WebSocketSubject's next() method to send messages.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the method accepts a string parameter and properly sends it using the WebSocketSubject's next() method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sendMessage method is not implemented correctly. Check that it's a public method with a string parameter that sends messages via the WebSocket connection.

steps.title: Implement connection cleanup
steps.instruction: Implement the OnDestroy interface in your WebSocketService and add the ngOnDestroy() method to close the WebSocket connection when the service is destroyed.
steps.hint: Import OnDestroy from '@angular/core', implement it in your service class, and define ngOnDestroy() to call unsubscribe() on your WebSocketSubject.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WebSocketService will implement proper cleanup by closing the WebSocket connection when the service is destroyed.
successCriteria: WebSocketService implements OnDestroy interface and has an ngOnDestroy() method that calls unsubscribe() on the WebSocketSubject.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've properly implemented the OnDestroy interface and added the ngOnDestroy() method with the unsubscribe call.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service doesn't yet implement proper cleanup. Remember to implement OnDestroy and add the ngOnDestroy() method to handle connection cleanup.

steps.title: Create main component and import service
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component class named 'WebSocketComponent' with the @Component decorator and inject the WebSocketService in its constructor.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the component metadata (e.g., selector, template). Import the WebSocketService and add it as a parameter in the constructor.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new component class is created with proper Angular decorator and service injection.
successCriteria: The component is named 'WebSocketComponent', uses @Component decorator, and injects WebSocketService in its constructor.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but check that it's named 'WebSocketComponent' and properly injects the WebSocketService.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Make sure to use @Component decorator and inject WebSocketService in the constructor.

steps.title: Initialize component state for messages
steps.instruction: In the WebSocketComponent class, define a property named 'messages' as an array of strings to store incoming WebSocket messages.
steps.hint: Add a public property with type string[] and initialize it as an empty array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a typed array property ready to store WebSocket messages.
successCriteria: The WebSocketComponent has a 'messages' property of type string[] initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure 'messages' is a public property with type string[] and initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the required 'messages' property. Add a string array property to store WebSocket messages.

steps.title: Subscribe to WebSocket messages in ngOnInit
steps.instruction: Implement the ngOnInit lifecycle hook in your WebSocketComponent to call the service's connect() method and subscribe to incoming messages, storing them in the messages array.
steps.hint: Add the OnInit interface, implement ngOnInit, and subscribe to the service's message observable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will automatically connect to the WebSocket and start receiving messages when it initializes.
successCriteria: ngOnInit is implemented, calls connect(), and subscribes to messages, storing them in the messages array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're implementing OnInit, calling connect(), and subscribing to store messages in the array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've implemented the ngOnInit lifecycle hook correctly with the required subscription logic.

steps.title: Create template to display messages and send input
steps.instruction: Update the component's template to display the messages array and add an input field with a send button that calls the service's sendMessage() method.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor to iterate over messages array, bind input value with [(ngModel)], and call sendMessage() on button click.
